analysis: Examined scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py (base text, both units) and its patch. The change is test-only: it adds a HOURLY = "ci-dev-hourly.yml" constant, adds that workflow to the set of classified workflows in test_every_workflow_is_classified (head ~line 709-710), and adds test_hourly_full_run_only_dispatches_ci_dev_on_dev (head ~959-977). That test pins the new workflow's triggers (schedule, workflow_dispatch), the cron '7 * * * *', the top-level `permissions: {}`, and the GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runner. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the remainder of that test, including any job-permission and dispatch-target assertions, is not visible. The new workflow file itself is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not check its permissions (it must be able to dispatch CI, which probably needs actions: write), its checkout/secrets use, or whether it really dispatches only ci-dev.yml on dev. The test adds a guard rather than weakening one: the existing UNROUTED/ROUTED checks still ensure release and credentialed workflows keep literal runners, that no workflow other than the router and the watchdog names self-hosted or darkbloom labels, and that the router stays isolated with empty permissions. Because the new workflow is not in UNROUTED, ROUTED or CALLERS, the "no self-hosted/darkbloom labels" loop in test_release_and_credentialed_workflows_keep_literal_runners will cover it. No provider-runtime threat-model assets (A-001..A-020, TB-002..TB-014) are touched; this is CI governance only. Remaining question for integration: confirm that ci-dev-hourly.yml, if included in the PR, grants minimal permissions and dispatches only the intended workflow and ref. No security regression is evidenced here.
